summary: 工作繁忙是否变成过载，可从睡眠、记忆和家庭生活的变化察觉。文章以经理人和创业者为例，说明人们为何容易高估未来的空闲，并提出重新审视工作量、获得支持和改善工作环境。
logic: 从长工时辨认预警信号
为何总会答应更多工作
压力的身心与经济代价
调整工作量与寻求支持

paragraphs.brief: 对大多数高级主管来说，工作量在极为繁忙和疯狂之间波动。
sentences: How busy is too busy?
忙到什么时候了？
For some it means sometimes having to have a short lunch; for others it may mean missing lunch altogether.
对一些人来说，这意味着有时必须吃一个短暂的午餐；对另一些人来说，这可能意味着完全没有吃午饭。
For a few, it is not being able to take a day off once a month.
对于少数人来说，它无法每月休一天假。
Then there is a group of people for whom working every evening and weekend is normal, and feeling stressed is taken for granted.
然后，有一群人每天晚上和周末工作都是正常的，感觉压力是理所当然的。
For most senior executives, workloads swing between extremely busy and frenzied.
对大多数高级主管来说，工作量在极为繁忙和疯狂之间波动。
Neil Plumridge, vice-president of a management consultancy company, says that his weeks vary from a ‘manageable’ 45 hours to 80 hours, but average 60 hours.
管理咨询公司的副总裁Neil Plumridge说，他的周数从 " 可管理 " 45小时到80小时不等，但平均为60小时。

paragraphs.brief: 他说：我知道事情是失控的。
sentences: Three signs warn Plumridge about his workload: sleep, scheduling and family.
三个迹象警告普卢姆里奇他的工作：睡眠、时间安排和家人。

He knows he is doing too much when he gets less than six hours’ sleep for three consecutive nights, when he is constantly having to reschedule appointments, and when he misses a family birthday or anniversary.
他知道，当他连续三个晚上睡眠不足6小时、经常要重新安排预约、错过家庭生日或周年纪念时，他就会做太多事。
‘Then,’ he says, ‘I know things are out of control.’
他说：我知道事情是失控的。
Plumridge states that stress is often caused by his having unrealistic expectations of himself.
Prumridge说，压力往往是因为他对自己抱有不切实际的期望。
‘I’ll promise a client that I’ll do something tomorrow, and then I’ll promise another client that I’ll do the same thing, when I know it’s not going to happen.
我答应一个客户明天我会做一些事情，然后我会答应另一个客户我会做同样的事情，当我知道它不会发生。
I could have said: “Why don’t I give that to you in 48 hours?”
我本可以说：“我为什么不在48小时内给你呢？”
The client wouldn’t care.’
客户不会在乎。

paragraphs.brief: 过度承诺是人们作为个人问题经历的问题。
sentences: Over-committing is something people experience as an individual problem.
过度承诺是人们作为个人问题经历的问题。
However, new research indicates that people may be designed to over-commit.
然而，新的研究表明，人们可能被设计成过度承诺。
A study in the Journal of Experimental Psychology shows that people always believe that they will be less busy in the future.
《实验心理学杂志》的一项研究表明，人们总是相信，他们今后会比较不忙。
This is a misapprehension according to the authors of the report, Gal Zauberman of the University of North Carolina and John Lynch of Duke University.
北卡罗来纳大学的Gal Zauberman和杜克大学的John Lynch认为，这是对报告的作者的误解。
‘On average, an individual will be just as busy two weeks or a month from now as he or she is today.
平均来说，一个人在两周或一个月后就会像现在一样忙。
But that is not how it appears in everyday life,’ they say.
他们说：这在日常生活中不是那样的。
‘People make commitments long in advance that they would never make if the same commitments required immediate action.
`人民早在承诺之前就作出承诺，如果同样的承诺需要立即采取行动，他们将永远也不会作出承诺。
They discount future time investments relatively steeply.’
它们相对而言对未来时间投资的低估幅度较大。

paragraphs.brief: 但对于任何个人来说，都有一些具体的压力迹象：睡眠不稳、身心健康下降是最常见的例子。
sentences: Being ‘too busy’ is highly subjective, but for any individual there are some concrete signs of stress: disturbed sleep and declining mental and physical health are the most common examples.
但对于任何个人来说，都有一些具体的压力迹象：睡眠不稳、身心健康下降是最常见的例子。

Figures for National Workers’ Compensation (insurance against injury caused by work) show that stress causes the most loss of time of any workplace injury: employees suffering stress are absent from work for an average of 16.6 weeks.
国家工人补偿(工伤保险)数字表明，压力造成任何工伤的时间损失最多：遭受压力的雇员平均16.6周不上班。
The effects of stress are also expensive.
压力的影响也是昂贵的。

The Australian Government insurer reports that, in 2003–2004, claims for stress-related psychological injury accounted for 7% of insurance claims, but almost 27% of the amount paid out in claim payments.
澳大利亚政府保险人报告说，2003-2004年，与压力有关的心理伤害索赔占保险索赔的7%，但几乎占索赔付款额的27%。

paragraphs.brief: 专家们说，处理压力的关键不是注重救济——高尔夫球赛或按摩——而是重新评估工作量。
sentences: Experts say the key to dealing with stress is not to focus on relief — a game of golf or a massage — but to reassess workloads.
专家们说，处理压力的关键不是注重救济——高尔夫球赛或按摩——而是重新评估工作量。
Neil Plumridge says he makes it a priority to work out what has to change: that might mean allocating extra staff to a job, allowing more time, or changing expectations.
Neil Plumridge说，他把解决必须改变的问题作为优先事项：这可能意味着分配额外工作人员从事一项工作，允许更多的时间，或改变期望。
He also relies on the advice of colleagues, saying that his peers coach each other on business problems: ‘Just a fresh pair of eyes over an issue can help,’ he states.
他说：“他还依赖同事的建议，他说他的同伴们在商业问题上互相指导：“只是一对对新人对一个问题的眼睛可以有所帮助。”

paragraphs.brief: 她的公司发展如此之快，以致于在2004年《商业评论周刊》上刊登了增长最快的小企业的“快100”名单，就在Stoykov生了第一个孩子之后。
sentences: Executive stress is not confined to big organisations.
行政压力不仅限于大型组织。
Vanessa Stoykov has been running her own advertising agency and public relations business for seven years.
Vanessa Stoykov经营自己的广告公司和公共关系业务已有七年。
Her company has grown so fast that it appeared on the Business Review Weekly ‘Fast 100’ list of fastest-growing small enterprises in 2004, just after Stoykov had her first child.
她的公司发展如此之快，以致于在2004年《商业评论周刊》上刊登了增长最快的小企业的“快100”名单，就在Stoykov生了第一个孩子之后。
In 2005, revenue was projected to double to $2.4 million.
2005年，收入预计翻一番，达到240万美元。
She had just had her second child.
她刚生了第二个孩子
With a fast-growing business and two small children, Stoykov says she has mastered the art of caring for children, typing, and talking on the phone at the same time.
Stoykov说，她掌握了照顾孩子、打字和同时在电话上聊天的艺术。
But, unlike many others, she appears to thrive on the mental stimulation of running her own business, despite the stress.
但是，与许多其他人不同的是，她似乎在精神刺激下兴旺地经营自己的企业，尽管压力很大。

paragraphs.brief: 执行辅导专业的心理学家Jan Elsner说，高级行政人员通常在繁重的工作量上表现良好。
sentences: Jan Elsner, a psychologist who specialises in executive coaching, says that doing well on a demanding workload is typical of senior executives.
执行辅导专业的心理学家Jan Elsner说，高级行政人员通常在繁重的工作量上表现良好。
Some people work best with high-adrenaline periods followed by quieter times, while others thrive under sustained pressure.
有些人工作最顺利的是高成人期，其次是较平静的时期，而其他人则在持续的压力下蓬勃发展。

Elsner’s practice is based on a movement known as positive psychology, a school of thought that argues that positive experiences — feeling engaged and challenged, for example — do not balance out negative experiences such as stress; instead they help people increase their resilience over time.
Elsner的实践是基于一种被称为积极心理学的运动，一种思想学派认为，积极的经验——例如感觉参与和受到挑战——不能平衡诸如压力等消极经历；相反，它们帮助人们随着时间的推移提高复原力。
Elsner says that many of the senior business people she coaches are increasingly relying more on regulating stress through methods such as meditation.
Elsner说，许多她辅导的资深商人越来越依赖通过冥想等方法来调节压力。
She points to research showing that meditation can alter the biochemistry of the brain and the way that brains and bodies react to stress.
她指出，研究显示冥想可以改变大脑的生物化学以及大脑和身体对压力的反应方式

paragraphs.brief: 最差的工作包括艰巨的工作和控制程度低。
sentences: Some experts believe there is too much emphasis on treating job stress as an individual problem.
一些专家认为，过于强调将工作压力作为个人问题处理。

Tony LaMontagne, of the University of Melbourne, says that while personality traits do have some effect on stress, it is systemic stressors — qualities of job roles and organisations themselves — that have a far greater effect.
墨尔本大学的Tony La Montagne说，虽然个性特征确实对压力有一定影响，但影响更大的是系统性压力——职务和组织本身的素质。
His recent research shows that the major predictor of stress is the level of job control a person has.
他最近的研究表明，压力的主要预测是一个人的工作控制水平。
The best type of job combines challenging work with high autonomy.
最佳的工作类型是具有挑战性的工作和高度自主性的工作。
The worst jobs combine challenging work and low control.
最差的工作包括艰巨的工作和控制程度低。
People with demanding jobs but little autonomy have up to four times the probability of depression and more than double the risk of heart attack.
工作要求高但几乎没有自主权的人，患抑郁症的可能性高达四倍，心脏病发作的风险也增加了一倍以上。

items.en: High-level workers tend to react positively to stress
items.zh: 高级工作人员往往对压力作出积极反应

items.zh: 通过讨好顾客，压力水平会提高

items.en: Support from other workers may relieve stress
items.zh: 其他工人的支助可以减轻压力

items.en: Lack of independence at work is often responsible for stress
items.zh: 工作缺乏独立性往往是造成压力的原因

items.en: Workers commonly expect their workloads to lessen over time
items.zh: 工人通常期望他们的工作量会随着时间的流逝而减少
items.answer: B · Gal Zauberman and John Lynch
items.solution: 加尔·祖伯曼和约翰·林奇

items.zh: 尼尔·普卢姆里奇没有提到以下哪些情况表明他的工作量太重？

更多休息时间参加体育活动或其他娱乐活动

items.en: According to Jan Elsner, meditation offers a method of
items.zh: 据Jan Elsner说，冥想提供了一种方法：
correct: changing the physical response to stress.
改变身体对压力的反应。

items.zh: 因压力请假的员工，平均离岗时间为________。
items.why: 直接给出因压力请假的平均时长。

items.en: This absence comes at a high price — while the number of insurance claims due to stress amount to only ________ of the total, they account for a much higher proportion of the cost of claim payments.

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空最多填两个词，可含数字。

pairs: 第 2 段 · 第 2 句
第 8 段 · 第 6 句
第 5 段 · 第 1 句
points: 摘要:“通过体育或等物理疗法寻求缓解可能不如…有效",对应 go/f oramassage,填 massage。
题干问“其他工人的支助可以减轻压力”。定位句写到“他说：“他还依赖同事的建议，他说他的同伴们在商业问题上互相指导：“只是一对对新人对一个问题的眼睛可以有所帮助。””。
clauses: Then there is a group of people … is normal, and feeling stressed is taken for granted.
“for whom working every evening and weekend”修饰前面的 group。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 whom 时，回看 group，再把修饰信息接回主句。
Neil Plumridge, vice-president of a management consultancy company, says ….
“that his weeks vary from a ‘manageable’ 45 hours to 80 hours, but average 60 hours”补足 says 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 says 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
